content.text: Asymmetrical PvP Game Project | Art Direction & 3D Environment Design

Developed in Unreal Engine, this project is a fast-paced, 1v1 asymmetrical PvP party game set within a chaotic, abandoned subway system. The gameplay pits a Hunter against a Monster in a tense game of evasion and psychological mind games, where the Monster attempts to corrupt the environment while the Hunter fights to preserve their Sanity (SAN) and intercept them.

As both the Art Director and the lead Environment Artist on this team project, my challenge was to establish a unified visual identity while driving the heavy lifting of the 3D production pipeline. On the directional side, I created comprehensive style guides to align our VFX, lighting, and animation artists, ensuring every asset reinforced the game’s core tension and mechanical readability.

On the production side, I personally designed and built the modular environment kits used to construct the subway system, utilizing a streamlined workflow in Maya and UE to craft the gritty, industrial architecture. To make the environment truly dynamic, I developed master materials and procedural texturing pipelines to handle the stark visual transition between reality and supernatural corruption. By closely bridging the gap between artistic vision and technical implementation in Unreal Engine, I managed asset optimization for real-time performance while ensuring our team delivered a beautifully atmospheric, high-pressure competitive arena.

As the Art Director and leader of this team project, my primary responsibility was to translate a fast-paced, high-concept gameplay hook into a cohesive, production-ready visual style. To align a multidisciplinary team of artists, I established a comprehensive visual bible and style guides that explicitly defined our target aesthetics: a hybrid of gritty, grounded realism for the industrial subway architecture and a vibrant, high-contrast palette for the supernatural corruption zones.

Leadership, to me, meant acting as the visual gatekeeper and the bridge between art and game design. I instituted daily stand-ups and regular asset review pipelines, ensuring that every animation, VFX, and lighting element directly served the game's strict mechanical readability requirements—such as ensuring the Monster remains distinct in dark tunnels and making the Hunter's declining Sanity visually unmistakable. By fostering an open, collaborative atmosphere, I guided our team through rapid prototyping phases, resolved creative bottlenecks, and maintained visual consistency across all departments. Ultimately, I ensured that the team delivered a highly polished, optimized, and atmospheric competitive arena on schedule within Unreal Engine.

On the production side, I was responsible for taking the subway environment from initial blockout to final, game-ready implementation inside Unreal Engine. To efficiently construct the sprawling, claustrophobic transit hub, I designed and modeled a comprehensive modular architectural kit using Maya and ZBrush. This included structural pillars, tiled wall panels, vaulted ceiling arches, and track assets that snapped perfectly to the grid, allowing for rapid layout iterations while keeping the draw-call count low.

I also took charge of prop scattering and set dressing to make the space feel lived-in and abandoned, while meticulously optimizing low-poly topologies, LODs (Level of Detail), and lightmaps to ensure the environment maintained a flawless, competitive frame rate without sacrificing atmospheric depth.

To complement the fast-paced gameplay, I designed the user interface with a strict focus on minimalism and high-contrast readability. The UI styling embraces an industrial, utilitarian aesthetic for the menus and HUD, which completely shifts when gameplay mechanics trigger state changes.

For the game’s marketing materials and promotional poster, my goal was to distill the entire asymmetric, psychological experience into a single, high-impact key art illustration. I composed the poster to emphasize the tense power dynamic of the cat-and-mouse chase, utilizing a dramatic Geometric Futurism composition within the subway tunnels. I established a stark visual contrast using a split color palette—juxtaposing the cool, dark, gritty tones of the industrial subway against the hot, glowing neon hue of the Monster’s corruption energy. This composition creates an immediate narrative hook, capturing the scale of the subterranean environment while instantly communicating the game’s core conflict to potential players.

Ultimately, my core mission on this project was Main Art Style Control—acting as the creative anchor to ensure that every environment asset, UI element, and piece of promotional art felt like it belonged to the exact same world. By establishing a definitive visual language that contrasted grounded, gritty industrial structuralism with vibrant, supernatural corruption, I successfully maintained stylistic cohesion across a multi-disciplinary team. Balancing high-level art direction, UI/UX design, and marketing art with hands-on 3D environment production allowed me to bridge the gap between creative vision and technical execution within Unreal Engine. This project stands as a testament to the power of structured leadership, cross-department collaboration, and intentional, gameplay-driven art design that elevates a fast-paced competitive experience from a mechanical prototype to an immersive, atmospheric reality.
Sci-Fi Industrial Environment | Modular Asset & Procedural Material Study

A sci-fi environment study exploring mood, lighting, and material storytelling. I focused on balancing hard-surface modeling with procedural texturing to create a believable yet stylized space. The scene aims to convey a quiet, immersive atmosphere through light, color, and composition.

This project follows a full environment pipeline using Blender and Maya for modeling, with UVs optimized in RizomUV. Procedural materials were created in Substance 3D Designer, with additional detailing in Substance 3D Painter. The scene was assembled and rendered in Unreal Engine 5, where I focused on lighting, material blending, and atmosphere to achieve a cohesive and immersive result.

Assets were designed with a modular workflow, focusing on reusability and consistency across the scene. Modeling was done in Blender and Maya, starting from blockout to refined hard-surface assets. UVs were optimized in RizomUV to ensure efficient texture usage. Procedural materials created in Substance 3D Designer provided a consistent base, while additional detailing in Substance 3D Painter added variation and storytelling elements.

Sci-fi materials were created in Substance 3D Designer using a procedural workflow. I began with primary and secondary shapes to define panel layouts and mechanical structure, then layered finer details to enhance surface complexity. Height information was used to generate normal and AO maps, ensuring strong depth and readability. Color and roughness maps were developed with subtle variation to simulate different surface conditions. Key parameters were exposed for flexibility and reuse.

The final cinematic focuses on creating a moody and immersive sci-fi atmosphere. Through controlled lighting, contrast, and color balance, the scene conveys a sense of quiet tension and subtle narrative. Soft ambient light combined with focused highlights helps guide the viewer’s attention while enhancing depth and spatial layering.
3D Character Design | High-Poly Sculpture & ZBrush

For the character asset, I executed the full high-poly production pipeline, focusing purely on 3D form, anatomy, and digital sculpting within ZBrush. The workflow began with a rigorous blockout phase, where I prioritized silhouette readability and proportions to ensure the character commands a strong visual presence within the game's environment.
The final high-poly sculpt serves as a highly detailed, polished foundation engineered to seamlessly transition into the texturing and game-ready baking pipelines.

The creation of this character followed a rigorous high-poly sculpting pipeline inside ZBrush, focusing on silhouette readability, structural anatomy, and clean mechanical execution. The process began with a geometric blockout to lock in core proportions and ensure a striking, instantly recognizable silhouette for the fast-paced gameplay. Next, the forms were fused using DynaMesh to sculpt the underlying anatomy, while SubTool extractions were used to build layered garments and realistic fabric folds. To align the asset with our game's industrial aesthetic, I utilized ZModeler and edge creasing to achieve crisp, hard-surface mechanical components. Finally, after optimizing the topology with ZRemesher, the model was subdivided to apply high-frequency tertiary details like structural seams and micro-surface wear, resulting in a highly polished, production-ready digital sculpture.

For the texturing phase, I established a Physically Based Rendering (PBR) pipeline within Substance Painter to seamlessly anchor the character into our game's environment. After baking the high-poly ZBrush details onto the optimized low-poly mesh, I focused on surface contrast by layering heavy, matte industrial fabrics alongside scratched metallic gear and glossy glass visors. Using smart masks and procedural generators, I carefully added realistic environmental wear.

Ultimately, this character asset serves as a testament to bridging high-level art direction with rigorous 3D execution. By controlling the entire pipeline—from the initial ZBrush silhouette blockout to the final PBR texture passes—I ensured the character perfectly embodies the project's industrial aesthetic.
Procedural Sci-Fi Material Collection | Substance 3D Designer

This project showcases a collection of procedural sci-fi materials created in Substance 3D Designer. The materials were inspired by real-world references and photographic textures, combining industrial realism with a futuristic sci-fi aesthetic. Each material was carefully developed to be modular, reusable, and adjustable, making it suitable for environment design and real-time applications. The collection includes a variety of surface types, such as metallic panels, worn machinery, industrial pipes, and mechanical components, all designed to convey depth, detail, and visual interest.

This project presents a simple sci-fi environment built entirely using my procedural material library, showcasing both the old and new versions of each material for comparison. It demonstrates a full asset and environment production workflow, from modeling to final scene assembly. This project showcases a simple sci-fi scene built using my procedural material library. Assets were modeled in Maya and UV-mapped in RizomUV, while all materials were created and refined in Substance 3D Designer and Painter. The scene was assembled in Unreal Engine 5, highlighting both old and new material versions to show iterative improvements and enhanced surface detail.

For this project, each material was created using Substance 3D Designer and Substance 3D Painter, producing two distinct versions: old and new. The old version followed the initial procedural setup, focusing on base shapes and basic surface details. The new version was iteratively refined with additional layers, enhanced edge wear, improved paneling, and color/roughness adjustments to increase realism and readability. This approach allowed a direct comparison, showcasing workflow improvements and the evolution of material quality.

The lace material was created in Substance 3D Designer by first defining the base pattern using tile generators and shape nodes to form the intricate lace motifs. Noise and curvature variations were layered to add subtle depth and imperfection, and height information was refined to enhance normal and ambient occlusion maps. Finally, roughness and color maps were adjusted to capture the delicate, semi-transparent look of lace while keeping the material procedural and easily adjustable.

The brick pattern was created in Substance 3D Designer by using tile generators to define the brick layout, combined with shape nodes and procedural masks to create cracks, grooves, and surface variation.

The final video presents the assembled sci-fi scene, showcasing the application of procedural materials in a real-time environment. It highlights the visual improvements between old and new material versions, as well as the overall atmosphere, lighting, and depth of the scene. Subtle highlights, reflections, and ambient lighting guide the viewer’s attention while emphasizing scale and surface detail.
Subsurface Scattering (SSS) Material with Moss & Plants | Substance 3D Designer & Painter

This project showcases a procedural subsurface scattering (SSS) material featuring plants and moss, designed to capture the delicate translucency and organic details of natural surfaces. The material was created to be versatile and adjustable, suitable for both close-up renders and real-time environment applications. In Substance 3D Designer, the base forms of moss and plant structures were created using procedural shapes, noise, and tile generators to define organic patterns and depth. Height and curvature maps were generated to drive SSS and surface variation. In Substance 3D Painter, additional color variation, subtle translucency adjustments, and fine details were applied, enhancing the perception of soft, semi-transparent organic surfaces. The final SSS effect was tested in real-time to ensure proper light diffusion and realistic shading.
Unreal Engine | Modeling, Animation & Visual Development

This project is a cinematic sequence created in Unreal Engine using Sequencer. All assets were self-designed and modeled, with animations crafted to support visual storytelling and motion. The focus was on composition, camera movement, and timing to create a cohesive cinematic experience. Lighting and materials were carefully refined to enhance mood and visual quality, resulting in a polished real-time sequence.

All models were designed and created from scratch, starting with concept sketches. High-poly models were made for detail, then optimized to low-poly for real-time use. UVs and materials were applied and tested in-engine before integration into the cinematic sequence.

The cinematic sequence was built in Unreal Engine using Sequencer. Cameras, animations, and timing were carefully arranged to tell a cohesive visual story. All animations, including character and environmental movements, were integrated and iteratively refined, with lighting and materials adjusted to enhance mood and cinematic impact.

The final video showcases the cinematic sequence, highlighting the environment, modeled assets, and animations in motion. It demonstrates camera work, lighting, and dynamic elements, giving a complete view of the scene and storytelling.
Stylized Sci-Fi Racing Track | Modular Level Design & Asset Development

This project is a racing game focused on speed, control, and player immersion. Players navigate through a variety of track environments, mastering acceleration, drifting, and timing to outperform opponents. The experience emphasizes responsive vehicle handling and dynamic gameplay, creating a balance between realism and arcade-style excitement.

Assets were created using a modular workflow, starting from reference and concept development. Models were optimized for real-time use, with procedural materials ensuring consistency and flexibility. The final environment was assembled in-engine, followed by lighting, composition, and performance optimization.

The level was built in Blueprint using a custom system I developed to streamline modular asset placement and track setup. This allowed for quick iteration and flexible adjustments. The scene was continuously tested and refined, focusing on flow, pacing, and overall player experience. Iterative playtesting helped improve navigation clarity and gameplay balance.

The level features obstacles, item pickups, and enemy elements to enhance challenge and gameplay variety. These systems were designed to support player interaction and pacing. The final video showcases the environment, gameplay, and overall experience in motion.
Gameplay Systems & Modular Blueprint Components | Item, Platform, Enemy & Trap Implementation

This project demonstrates a complete set of gameplay functions implemented through modular Blueprint Components in Unreal Engine, including collectible items like score and health pickups, moving and rotating platforms, enemies with auto-tracking or fixed turrets, spinning saw hazards, traps such as mines and explosive triggers, and scoring systems for coins and stars. Each component is designed for reuse, enabling dynamic interactions, flexible level design, and modular, scalable gameplay mechanics suitable for prototypes or full game development.

PROJECT 01 Key Features:Item Pickups: Players can collect various items, with logic handled by modular blueprints.Scoring & Counting Mechanics: Tracks player progress and updates scores in real time.Interactive Treasure Chests: Blueprints manage chest interactions and reward delivery.Player Health Management: Health bars and damage logic provide immediate feedback to the player. Design Approach: Each system is modular and reusable, designed to support dynamic interactions, deliver clear player feedback, and serve as the foundation for more complex gameplay features.

This video showcases the core gameplay systems implemented with Blueprint Components, highlighting item pickups, scoring mechanics, interactive treasure chests, and player health management. It demonstrates how each system responds dynamically to player interactions, with real-time feedback through score updates, health bar changes, and chest rewards. The video also illustrates the modular design of the blueprints, showing how these foundational mechanics can be easily reused and adapted for different levels or gameplay scenarios.

PROJECT 02 Swinging obstacles that damage the player on contact, with modular movement and collision logic.Damage-Dealing Enemies: Enemies designed to inflict harm through contact or attack patterns.Fixed Hazards: Static traps that continuously pose danger in the level, such as spikes or crushing elements.Moving Platforms: Multi-path and dynamic platforms that challenge player navigation and timing. Design Approach: All systems are modular and reusable, allowing flexible placement and combination within different levels. The blueprints support dynamic interactions and provide clear visual and gameplay feedback, forming the core mechanics for challenging level design.

The video demonstrates these enemy and hazard systems in action, showcasing pendulum and damage-dealing enemies, fixed traps, and moving platforms interacting with the player. It highlights the modularity and flexibility of the blueprint components, emphasizing both gameplay challenge and level design versatility.

PROJECT 03 Projectiles that automatically track and follow the player, with modular targeting and movement logic.Projectile Weapons: Various fired objects with customizable speed, trajectory, and damage properties.Turret Variants: Includes auto-tracking turrets, fixed turrets, and rotating turrets, each with independent attack and targeting behaviors.Damage Handling: All projectiles and turrets integrate with player health systems for responsive feedback. Design Approach: Blueprint components are modular and reusable, enabling easy adaptation of turrets and projectile behaviors across multiple levels. The system emphasizes dynamic interactions, tactical gameplay challenge, and scalability for more complex combat mechanics.

The video showcases different turret types, homing missiles, and projectile attacks interacting with the player. It demonstrates modular blueprint implementation, highlighting how each component can be combined to create engaging and varied combat scenarios.

This project integrates all previously developed gameplay components into a single 2D side-scrolling game, featuring item pickups, scoring, treasure chests, health management, pendulum and damage enemies, moving platforms, projectile systems, and turret variants. It combines these mechanics into a cohesive gameplay experience, enhanced by a distinctive stylized visual design and visual effects, modular blueprint architecture for reusable and flexible level design, and clear UI feedback systems including health bars, score counters, and interactive indicators to improve player experience.

The video showcases the fully integrated side-scrolling game in action, highlighting item pickups, enemy interactions, moving platforms, projectile attacks, and stylized UI elements. It demonstrates the modularity of the components and the cohesive gameplay experience created by combining all prior systems.

UE PCG Systems | Spline, Density, and Procedural Content Implementation
An Unreal Engine PCG study covering spline-based terrain, procedural vegetation, modular Blueprints, and performance optimization.
A procedural vegetation study using splines, density controls, point placement, and reusable Blueprint systems.
Custom PCG graphs and tools extend the system into a flexible workflow for dynamic environment generation.
Unity Shader Systems | Shader Graph, Lighting, and Stylized Rendering

This project focuses on creating stylized shaders in Unity using Shader Graph and applying them within a real-time game scene. It includes custom shaders, material setups, and their integration across environment assets to achieve a cohesive visual style. The workflow combines shader development with lighting and rendering adjustments to enhance both visual quality and performance.

This part presents a stylized game environment with a focus on cartoon rendering and shader development in Unity. The visual style is driven by custom shaders created with Shader Graph, emphasizing simplified lighting, bold color control, and non-photorealistic shading. Shaders were designed to enhance surface readability and artistic expression, and were applied across the scene to maintain a consistent stylized look. Combined with lighting and post-processing, the project highlights the integration of technical shader work and visual design to achieve a cohesive cartoon-style environment.

This scene explores a stylized environment with an emphasis on cartoon-style rendering and shader variation. Custom shaders were developed in Unity using Shader Graph to create distinct material responses, including soft shading transitions, controlled highlights, and simplified shadow behavior. Different shaders were applied to various assets to introduce visual contrast while maintaining overall stylistic consistency. Through adjustments in lighting, color grading, and material parameters, the scene achieves a balanced look that combines artistic stylization with real-time rendering performance.
GenerativeAI  | 3DArt | DigitalContentCreation

This project explores how generative AI can be integrated into a traditional 3D production pipeline to create a more efficient, controllable, and repeatable creative workflow. Rather than relying on a single AI model, I designed a modular pipeline that combines Blender, ComfyUI, MidJourney, GPT, Unreal Engine, and AI coding agents.

This project explores how generative AI can be integrated into a traditional 3D production pipeline to create a more efficient, controllable, and repeatable creative workflow. Rather than relying on a single AI model, I designed a modular pipeline that combines Blender, ComfyUI, MidJourney, GPT, Unreal Engine, and AI coding agents.
The workflow begins with structured 3D modeling in Blender, where geometry provides accurate spatial information. Using ComfyUI and ControlNet, depth maps and custom node-based workflows guide AI image generation while maintaining the original composition. MidJourney is then used to enhance visual style, and GPT assists with prompt optimization, workflow refinement, and iterative design decisions. After concept generation, AI tools such as Tripo AI and Hunyuan 3D are used to create 3D assets, followed by AI-assisted texture generation for higher-quality PBR materials. Finally, all assets are assembled in Unreal Engine, where procedural content generation (PCG), APIs, MCP, and AI coding agents help automate scene construction, improve production efficiency, and accelerate iteration.
Through this project, I learned not only how to use individual AI tools, but also how to design custom node-based workflows, integrate multiple AI systems, and combine them with traditional 3D production techniques. The primary objective is to transform AI from a probabilistic image generator into a controllable, modular, and production-ready pipeline for professional digital content creation.

As a 3D artist, I naturally approach concept design from a modeling perspective rather than relying solely on text prompts. Instead of generating images from scratch, I first create a simple 3D blockout in Blender to establish the composition, scale, and spatial relationships. Using the Blender–ComfyUI integration, I extract depth information and combine it with ControlNet to guide AI image generation while preserving the original structure. I then use MidJourney to refine the artistic style and GPT to optimize prompts and iterate on the results. This workflow transforms AI image generation from a random process into a controllable and repeatable design pipeline.

I also researched and tested different AI models to understand their unique visual styles, strengths, and generation characteristics. By comparing their results, I was able to identify which models and combinations best supported my creative goals and build a workflow that was more suitable for my own 3D design process.

For 3D asset generation, I built a workflow that combines multiple AI models to improve both efficiency and quality. I start with simple 3D geometry in Blender and use the Blender–ComfyUI plugin to generate three to five concept variations while preserving the original shape. Instead of relying on a single model, I use MidJourney as a style reference to provide a consistent visual direction. The generated concepts are then sent to GPT, where prompts are refined and the strongest ideas are combined into a final, higher-quality concept image. Finally, I use Adobe Firefly for additional editing and fine-tuning before moving to the next stage. This workflow allows me to batch-create multiple asset variations while keeping the overall design language consistent and significantly reducing iteration time.

To efficiently produce a large number of props, I developed a batch asset generation workflow. Starting from simple 3D blockouts, I generated multiple concept variations for different prop shapes using Blender and the ComfyUI integration. Once the concepts were finalized, I used AI-based 3D generation tools such as Tripo AI and Hunyuan 3D to quickly convert the concepts into initial 3D models. However, during testing, I found that while these one-click AI generation tools produced geometry efficiently, the texture quality was often inconsistent and lacked the level of detail required for production. To address this limitation, I continued exploring ComfyUI and built a dedicated AI texture generation workflow to improve PBR texture quality, including normal, roughness, and ambient occlusion maps. This allowed me to combine the speed of AI model generation with a more controllable texture pipeline, producing assets that were better suited for professional 3D production.

This workflow summarizes the development process of the AI-assisted 3D texture pipeline. I first studied the fundamentals of AI-generated 3D assets and explored commercial tools such as Tripo, node-based workflows in ComfyUI with HY3D, open-source solutions including the StableGen Blender add-on, and related research on AI 3D texture generation. Throughout the project, I also used GPT, Gemini, Codex, Claude, Blender, and Substance 3D Painter for research, coding, workflow optimization, and production. After multiple iterations in ComfyUI and StableGen, I integrated the findings into a custom AI texture plugin for Substance Painter, creating a more efficient and production-ready texture generation workflow.

Through studying the StableGen plugin, I first realized that AI texture generation could be integrated directly into a 3D application. More importantly, I learned the fundamental workflow behind most AI-based 3D texture generation systems. The process typically begins by capturing multiple views of a 3D model with virtual cameras. These views, together with depth maps and ControlNet-based guidance, provide the AI with structural information about each surface. The model then generates textures for each view from text prompts, and the results are projected back onto the 3D model and blended into a complete texture. This projection-based multi-view workflow forms the core logic behind most current AI texture generation methods.

The plugin provides two complementary texture generation workflows. The first uses multi-view image projection, allowing users to generate textures from reference images with adjustable projection angles, image offsets, projection parameters, and selectable view presets (6, 10, or 16+ views) for different model complexities. The second integrates ComfyUI for AI-driven texture generation, enabling users to control prompts, negative prompts, sampling steps, and other generation parameters to produce high-quality PBR textures within a flexible and efficient workflow.

The plugin was developed with the assistance of AI coding agents, including Claude and Codex, which were used for code generation, debugging, and workflow optimization. It communicates with the Adobe Substance 3D Painter API to integrate directly into the application, while the plugin itself is implemented using Python and JSON configuration files within the Substance Painter plugin framework, enabling a flexible and extensible architecture.

For the scene assembly stage, I first build the overall environment manually in Unreal Engine to establish the composition, lighting, atmosphere, and visual direction. After defining the main look, I use AI coding agents such as Claude and Codex to assist with scene expansion and lightweight development tasks. These agents help me create functional components, procedural tools, dynamic sky systems, material variations, and other interactive or technical features. The goal of this stage is to explore how AI agents can work alongside traditional tools such as Unreal Engine and Blender, not to replace the artist, but to accelerate repetitive tasks and support areas that require light coding or technical implementation. Through this process, I am continuing to test different AI agents and build a more flexible, efficient, and integrated 3D production workflow.

After assembling the scene in Unreal Engine, I render my own compositions from different camera angles and lighting setups. These renders become the foundation for further AI-assisted exploration. Instead of generating completely new scenes, I use my existing environment and selected camera views as references, allowing AI to produce multiple atmosphere variations, lighting conditions, and visual moods while preserving the original composition. These AI-generated references help me quickly explore creative directions and provide high-quality visual targets that I can bring back into Unreal Engine for further refinement. This creates an iterative workflow where traditional 3D production and AI continuously support and improve each other.

Traditionally, after completing an environment in Unreal Engine, I would manually create and keyframe a full set of cinematic cameras—including wide, medium, and close-up shots from multiple angles—to produce the final showcase video. To streamline this repetitive process, I developed a custom Unreal Engine camera automation plugin that generates a complete camera shot set based on user-defined requirements, such as shot type, viewing angle, framing, and camera movement. The generated cameras and shots are automatically organized into a Level Sequence, allowing a finished 3D environment to be quickly transformed into a structured cinematic presentation. This tool significantly reduces manual camera setup and enables an almost one-click workflow from completed environment to final showcase sequence.

This project has been successfully completed as my thesis project. It integrates AI-assisted texture generation, procedural workflows, and traditional 3D production into a unified pipeline. The result demonstrates a more efficient, scalable, and production-ready workflow for AI-assisted 3D content creation.

I extended the 3D environment into a short cinematic narrative using node-based AI video generation workflows. Building on my original scene design, I used AI video tools to explore cinematic camera movement, character performance, and visual storytelling, transforming the environment from a static 3D scene into a dynamic narrative experience.
GenerativeAI  | AIVideo | CinematicDesign

This project explores an end-to-end AI filmmaking workflow, covering every stage from story development to final video production. The process begins with script writing, story development, and storyboard design. MidJourney is used to establish the visual style and generate key concept frames, while Runway, Higgsfield, and other AI video generation tools create cinematic shots and motion sequences. Each tool is selected for its strengths, allowing different parts of the production to achieve the best possible quality. Finally, all generated assets are integrated and organized in LTX Studio to build a complete narrative with consistent pacing, transitions, and visual storytelling. The project demonstrates how multiple AI models can work together to create a complete cinematic production pipeline, from initial concept to the final short film.

The story was entirely written and designed by me. Inspired by my interest in science fiction films, I created two opposing extraterrestrial civilizations and built the narrative around their long-standing conflict and history. The screenplay follows a classic three-act Hollywood structure: an opening that establishes the world and characters, a rising conflict leading to the climax, and a final twist that redefines the meaning of the story.
At the center of the narrative is the concept of Karma, symbolized by a single flower that appears throughout the film. Rather than focusing only on action or spectacle, the story explores the cycle of cause and consequence, using the conflict between the two civilizations to express an anti-war message. Through this symbolic narrative, I wanted to emphasize that violence ultimately leads to another cycle of suffering, making the film not only a science fiction story but also a reflection on humanity and conflict.

To develop the visual world of the film, I combined multiple AI models, including MidJourney, Nobanana, GPT, Higgsfield, and Runway, with each tool contributing its own strengths to the creative process. Rather than relying on a single model, I explored different AI systems to generate high-quality concept art, characters, environments, and cinematic references. The story is set on an ancient alien planet, featuring two opposing civilizations with distinct cultures, architecture, costumes, and visual identities. Throughout this stage, I generated multiple viewpoints and design variations for every major character, environment, and prop. These high-quality references established a consistent visual language and provided a strong foundation for the later stages of AI video production and shot generation.

After completing the AI storyboard, character designs, environment concepts, and keyframes, I bring all of these assets into TyperNow for final video production. The keyframes place the characters inside the designed environments and define the exact camera angle, composition, and visual moment that must appear in each shot. TyperNow provides a node-based production system where I can connect different images, assign reference frames, write prompts, and organize the entire generation process within one interface. This allows me to manage the relationship between characters, environments, camera movement, and shot continuity more clearly. I also use AI coding tools such as Claude to help develop more specific prompts for different shots, improving motion quality, consistency, and cinematic control throughout the final video.

To maintain visual consistency throughout the film, I generate a large library of reference images for every important element, including characters, environments, props, costumes, and symbolic objects such as the flower that represents Karma. Rather than relying only on text prompts, I reference these images through the node-based workflow during every stage of video generation. Each shot can reuse the same visual references for characters, scenes, and key props, significantly improving consistency across different generations. This approach helps preserve character identity, environment design, and prop details throughout the entire film, making the final result feel much more coherent and production-ready.

During video generation, I use three layers of control to make the results as consistent as possible. First, I create a camera layout that defines the position and movement of the camera throughout each shot. Second, I design detailed storyboards and keyframes that specify the exact composition, framing, and visual moment for every scene. Finally, I use carefully engineered prompts, refined with Claude, to describe the desired camera motion, lighting, character actions, and cinematic style. By combining camera planning, storyboard references, and structured prompts, I can significantly reduce the randomness of AI video generation. After generating multiple versions of each shot, I select the strongest results and assemble them through editing to produce the final cinematic sequence.

After the AI video generation stage, I complete the project through post-production and editing. Instead of relying on a single AI-generated result, I generate multiple versions of each shot and carefully select the strongest takes, the smoothest motion, and the most coherent sequences. These clips are then edited together using professional video editing software such as CapCut and Adobe Premiere Pro to improve pacing, shot continuity, and overall cinematic quality.
For audio production, I use AI tools such as ElevenLabs and Claude to generate background music, sound effects, and custom audio elements that match the atmosphere of each scene. Finally, all visual and audio assets are combined through the editing process, resulting in a complete cinematic short film with consistent storytelling, visual quality, and sound design.
Vibe Coding |  Website Rebrand  | Visual Desgin

Rebranding and redevelopment of an AI agent company website. Starting from the original website, I conducted market and visual research, redesigned the brand identity, and rebuilt the entire website using AI-generated images, videos, 3D assets, and modern web coding workflows. The project leveraged Codex, Claude, and AI-assisted development tools to deliver a complete end-to-end website experience.

Before starting the redesign, I analyzed over 50 AI and technology company websites to identify common visual patterns and design trends. The research focused on color usage, typography, layout, and overall visual style, providing a clear direction for the rebranding and ensuring the final design aligned with current industry standards.

To accelerate the creative process, AI tools were extensively used throughout the website redesign, including logo rebranding, visual assets, hero images, landing-page animations, and promotional videos. I defined the overall creative direction and visual style, while AI tools were used to generate and iterate the final assets. The workflow combined GPT, Gemini, Nobanana, AI image generation models, Runway, Hailuo AI, and other AI video generation tools to efficiently produce high-quality visual content.

The website was developed using an AI-assisted web coding workflow powered by Codex and Claude. I first established the overall website architecture, user flow, and interaction logic before building the core framework. Once the structure was complete, I integrated AI-generated videos, animations, and visual assets to create dynamic backgrounds and interactive experiences. After confirming that all content and functionality were in place, I refined the details by replacing placeholder assets with higher-quality images, videos, and animations. This project focuses on developing an AI-assisted Digital Twin system for the mining industry. The workflow begins with comprehensive research into a real mining site, including its geographic location, operational processes, equipment, and production workflow. Based on this research, AI tools are used to generate 3D assets and environmental components, which are then assembled in Unreal Engine to recreate the mining environment. Building on the scene, AI coding agents such as Claude, Codex, and MCP are used to develop interactive features, including camera control, UI systems, and real-time data connections. The final goal is to create an interactive Digital Twin platform that visualizes mining operations and supports real-time monitoring, data visualization, and intelligent user interaction.

he project uses Unreal Engine as the central production platform. Cesium provides real-world GIS terrain and geospatial data, creating an accurate foundation for the mining environment. AI-generated concept images are used to design the required equipment and assets, while Tripo AI and Hunyuan 3D accelerate the initial 3D model generation process. Blender is used for model adjustment, cleanup, and asset preparation before the models are imported into Unreal Engine for scene assembly.

The complete software pipeline is: research and GIS data → Cesium and Unreal Engine → AI concept generation → Tripo AI or Hunyuan 3D → Blender optimization → Unreal Engine scene assembly → PCG and AI-agent development → UI and real-time data integration → interactive mining Digital Twin.

The project begins with research on a real mining site in Colorado. We first study the site's geographic location, mining operations, equipment, and production workflow to understand how the environment functions in the real world. Since the project is based on a real location, accurate GIS data is essential. We use the Cesium plugin in Unreal Engine to stream high-quality geospatial data and terrain directly into the engine. This provides a realistic digital foundation that matches the real-world environment. Based on this GIS data, we continue building the mining site, placing assets, and developing the complete Digital Twin workflow inside Unreal Engine.

The early research stage focuses on understanding how a real mining site operates. This includes studying the complete industrial process, from mineral extraction and transportation to crushing, screening, grinding, and final processing. Each stage must follow the actual operational sequence used in the real mine, including the corresponding industrial machinery, equipment layout, and connections between different production areas. Based on this research, the entire mining workflow is reconstructed in 3D as accurately as possible, creating a one-to-one digital representation of the real production process for the Digital Twin system.

The asset creation process is also driven by real-world research. Based on the mining workflow, we first collect references for different types of industrial machinery and equipment using AI-assisted research. AI image generation is then used to produce higher-quality reference images from multiple viewpoints, giving us more complete design information than traditional image searches. These references are used as the input for AI 3D generation tools, such as Tripo AI and Hunyuan 3D, to rapidly create the initial 3D assets. The generated models are further refined in Blender when necessary before being imported into Unreal Engine. Finally, these optimized assets are assembled into the Digital Twin environment according to the real mining process and equipment layout, ensuring both visual accuracy and consistency with the actual industrial workflow.

The complete environment assembly was carried out by me. Based on real mining references and research, I analyzed each stage of the industrial workflow and recreated it step by step in Unreal Engine. I determined where each piece of equipment should be placed, how the different production areas should connect, and how materials move through the site from extraction to processing. My responsibility was not only to make the scene visually convincing, but also to ensure that its layout and workflow accurately reflected the operation of a real mining site.

All assets in the environment were created and placed according to real-world mining references. I first completed the main scene assembly manually in Unreal Engine, including the terrain, industrial equipment, production areas, and the spatial relationships between different stages of the mining process. After the environment was established, I used AI coding agents such as Claude and Codex through MCP to assist with lightweight development tasks. These included camera controls for presenting different parts of the site, UI systems for displaying equipment and operational information, and other interactive functions. This integration made the development process faster and more efficient while allowing me to remain in control of the overall design and implementation.
